days.title: Massif Peaks and State Forests
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: foresta demaniale
stops.detail: The coal tit (Periparus ater) and the rarer marsh tit (Poecile palustris) also nest in wooded areas, especially beech forests and the silver fir woods of the state forest.

stops.name: ambienti rupestri
stops.detail: Rocky environments, high-altitude meadows and pastures are flown over by the common raven (Corvus corax), skylark (Alauda arvensis), black redstart (Phoenicurus ochruros) and swallows (Hirundinidae).

days.title: Beech Forests and Hillside Villages
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: faggete
stops.detail: At the level of springs and wetlands at lower altitudes the Italian tree frog (Hyla intermedia) is present while, instead, just about everywhere in the beech forests and along pools, springs and streams, the Apennine frog (Rana italica) is found.

stops.name: borghi collinari
stops.detail: On the side of anthropization, the presence of the hillside villages and the lifestyle in harmony with the territory favor species with a more plastic ecology.

days.title: Oak Groves and Waterways
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: querceti
stops.detail: The sub-mountain environment, thanks also to acorns and other fruits of the oak groves and mixed woods, is the habitat of the hazel dormouse (Muscardinus avellanarius).

stops.name: corsi d'acqua
stops.detail: The banks of the watercourses instead constitute an ideal habitat for the water vole (Arvicola amphibius).
